messages.subject: How to De-Risk the Personal Guarantee
messages.text_excerpt:
https://acquiringminds.co/

** How to De-Risk the Personal Guarantee

------------------------------------------------------------

Brendan Burdette and Ryan Conner have launched personal guarantee insurance to enable more — and stronger — SBA buyers.

How to Build a Franchise Holdco

https://acquiringminds.co/webinars/anatomy-of-a-franchise-holdco

Franchises and ETA play so well together.

In this webinar, Connor Groce covers:

* Single-brand roll-ups vs. multi-brand portfolios

* Franchise acquisitions: sourcing, diligence, and integration

* Institutional capital in franchising

* Industries with the most opportunity in franchising

* Case studies

Connor Groce has owned or operated franchise units in multiple systems.

He has grown his own portfolio through multiple successful acquisitions and learned the power that acquisitions can play in long-term value creation.

Watch this recorded webinar to learn from an expert at the intersection of ETA and franchising.

Watch Recording (free) (https://acquiringminds.co/webinars/anatomy-of-a-franchise-holdco)

The personal guarantee has long been a nonstarter for certain searchers who would otherwise jump at the opportunity to buy a business with an SBA loan.

And in many cases, such searchers are higher net worth, older, more seasoned and so actually pretty well qualified to succeed at business ownership.

But the prospect of losing their assets, their home, is just too much risk to accept. Understandably.

Well today's guests have launched an insurance product to help mitigate this risk:

Personal guarantee insurance, or PGI.

‍Brendan Burdette and Ryan Conner have founded Braddock Road Insurance Corporation, or BRIC, to bring PGI to the SBA business buyer market.

And they're not alone; another startup is due to launch their PGI product in the months ahead.

And by the way, this isn't pie-in-the-sky; PGI already exists in the UK and other markets.

So watch this space. If PGI takes off here, the effect on our market could be dramatic, and could finally enable those of you who would stay on the sidelines to get in the game.

** Key Takeaways

------------------------------------------------------------

1. Braddock Road Insurance Corporation (BRIC) has launched personal guarantee insurance (PGI) to address the major pain point of personal guarantees that prevent many would-be SBA business buyers from entering the market, particularly higher net worth, more seasoned entrepreneurs who have significant assets at risk.

2. The founders, Brendan Burdette and Ryan Conner, developed this product after experiencing the psychological burden of personal guarantees firsthand, with Connor having previously held a $2.7 million personal guarantee that caused him to lose sleep nightly and prevented them from pursuing their own SBA acquisition.

3. The insurance product covers 50% of the personal guarantee liability, meaning if a $2 million SBA loan defaults after corporate asset liquidation, BRIC would pay $1 million directly to the lender, reducing the borrower's personal exposure from the full amount to half while maintaining skin-in-the-game incentives.

4. Brendan and Ryan couldn't comment on pricing, but industry chatter estimates an annual policy cost of approximately 1-2% of loan value, or approximately $1,000-$2,000 per month per $1 million of loan. Premiums decrease over time as the loan balance is paid down, and borrowers can discontinue coverage if their business performs well and they no longer need the protection.

5. The product addresses the psychological barrier that has kept qualified entrepreneurs on the sidelines for years, with examples including second-generation entrepreneurs reluctant to risk family wealth built through previous SBA loans, and experienced professionals with families unwilling to put their homes at risk despite being well-suited to run businesses successfully.

** Watch the full video 👇👇

------------------------------------------------------------

Here are Ryan Conner and Brendan Burdette, founders of BRIC.
